method: All observation rows and all ordered actor/log assertions are read; full raw observations remain bound by SHA-256. No outliers are trimmed.
Positive shot-counter transitions define discharges; last_shot_time is the discharge time, not the later observation time. The actual OpenLevel counter reset is excluded.
Stage21 measures held fire; stage31 computes N-1 intervals between N full-magazine discharges. Observed RPM is60*(N-1)/(last-first), without reload time.
Nominal configured RPM is600/690. The runtime serializes its actual floating interval in the passing cadence assertion; phase errors use that interval and the first actual discharge.
Observation-frame gaps and complete ordinary game-frame interval summaries expose frame quantization. Requested caps are independently matched to log console readbacks.
Stages220-222 inject a320ms stall, then test one recovery discharge and a short no-catchup guard ending at deliberate key flush. No longer recovery interval is inferred.
limitations: Functional engine-component timing only: no native mouse-to-photon, audio audition, visual approval, performance or isolated-host claim.
Input normally enters SetTrigger directly; a late-tap hook follows actor tick, and focus cleanup uses the controller. Actual native input is separate evidence.
CSV times have six decimal places and runtime interval labels have nine; microsecond rounding remains in summaries, including negative near-zero tap/phase differences.
Only these three completed cadence runs are certified here. A larger driver session may still be running; its snapshot hash is retained without claiming that other modes passed.
Exact-source runtime verification is supplied by the fresh-build record and pre/post verified runner results. This offline curator does not rehash binaries or launch any process.
